scope: Idealized closed-loop simulation of the actual browser engine, mode D, left ear reported. Flat 50 dB HL audiogram, NAL-R gains, linear (1:1) compression, 4 ms forward delay, 65 dB SPL assumed input level, measured KEMAR HRIRs. Synthetic, time-invariant two-resonance feedback path (not measured) that fits inside the 64-tap canceller, no microphone noise or transducer nonlinearity: added stable gain is therefore an upper bound for this model, not a device result. Sweep -40 to +10 dB path gain in 2.5 dB steps; a value at the sweep edge means the limit was not reached. Stability judged on the last 5 s of 10 s. Magnitude-bound MSG ignores the loop phase condition and is conservative.

speech_in_noise.note: speech 0 deg + stationary noise 90 deg, 10 dB SNR
